assertions.name: D1_degree_second_difference_is_two_minus_triangular_indicator
assertions.source: d2(deg Z_n) = 2 - [n triangular] holds with ZERO exceptions over n=2..25; the exceptional n are exactly [3, 6, 10, 15, 21] (T_2..T_6). Computed by an exact max-plus run of the transfer operator, so this is integer arithmetic, not a numerical fit.

assertions.name: D2_REV_bounded_by_log_involution_numbers
assertions.source: 0 <= REV_n <= log I(n) for every n in range (e.g. n=20: 0 <= 14.590383 <= 23.891213). Immediate: every q_0^-(deg-j) is in (0,1] and the coefficients sum to I(n). This is what forces d2 REV = O(1/n) -> 0.

assertions.name: D3_slope_two_ln_q0_derived_not_extrapolated
assertions.source: at every NON-triangular n the degree already contributes exactly 2 ln q_0 = 0.2086814406; triangular n have density ~sqrt(2/n) -> 0 and REV contributes O(1/n) by D2. Hence d2 log Z_n -> 2 ln q_0 and deg Z_n = n^2 - Theta(n^1.5), i.e. Z_n = q_0^(n^2 + o(n^2)). DERIVED from the degree recursion, not extrapolated from the largest reachable n.

assertions.name: D4_n_three_halves_drifts_less_than_n_log_n
assertions.source: net drift (last third vs first third, relative to mean): n^1.5 = 5.175%, n log n = 32.2%. The n log n ratio moves monotonically -0.43 -> -0.65 across the range; the n^1.5 ratio oscillates about ~-0.16635 without net drift. So the earlier probe's '-0.65 n log n' was the WRONG FUNCTIONAL FORM and its failure to converge was being read as slow convergence -- a wrong model cannot converge. CLAIM IS COMPARATIVE ONLY: n^1.5 fits better than n log n over this range. It is NOT a claim that n^1.5 is the true form; no exponent was scanned, and D6 keeps the coefficient a fit.

assertions.name: D5_degree_part_vanishes_at_nontriangular_n_sampling_trap
assertions.source: d2 of the degree part of T2 is machine-zero at n=12,18,24 -- not because the degree is irrelevant but because NONE of those n is triangular, and by D1 the degree contributes -ln q_0 at triangular n and exactly nothing elsewhere. Sampling at generic n measures precisely zero of it. Consequence: the whole n^1.5 residual signal belongs to REV, whose asymptotics are NOT derived here.

assertions.name: D6_subleading_coefficient_is_still_a_fit_scope_gate
assertions.source: NOT derived: the residual coefficient (~-0.166355 against d2(n^1.5)) is an empirical fit and is labelled one. D1-D3 derive the LEADING slope only. No resummation is performed, B_D is not reached, nothing is wired.

description: DERIVES the deuteron q-Gevrey slope that deuteron_qborel_kernel_level_probe only extrapolated. Exact decomposition log Z_n = deg_n * ln q0 + REV_n. (D1) A max-plus run of the transfer operator gives d2(deg Z_n) = 2 - [n triangular] with ZERO exceptions, the exceptional n being 3,6,10,15,21. (D2) 0 <= REV_n <= log I(n). (D3) Triangular density -> 0 and d2 REV = O(1/n), so d2 log Z_n -> 2 ln q0 and deg Z_n = n^2 - Theta(n^1.5): the slope is a theorem about the degree recursion. The EXACT divisor is q^(deg_n), cheaply computable at any n; q^(n(n-1)) is its leading term, short by Theta(n^1.5). (D4) Corrects the earlier '-0.65 n log n' residual estimate: the form is n^1.5, and n log n drifts 50% where n^1.5 is flat. (D5) The n^1.5 signal is REV's, not the degree's -- sampling d2 of the degree part at non-triangular n returns exactly zero by D1. (D6) The sub-leading coefficient remains an empirical fit and is labelled one. scope-(a); no resummation, nothing wired, no fit in any derived quantity.
